intended_object: An auxiliary linear functional x ↦ det(q−p, x) on the plane, whose kernel is the line through 0 parallel to q−p. It is used only to build the affine function cutting out the line through an edge of a polygonal circle (from the docstring and its use in `edgeLine`).
explanation: The body is the planar cross product with the edge vector: x ↦ (q−p)₀x₁ − (q−p)₁x₀ = det(q−p, x). Its kernel is ℝ·(q−p), as the docstring says; when p = q it is the zero functional, a harmless degenerate case. Its only role is in the same file: `edgeLine` uses it to write the affine map x ↦ edgeNormalLinear(vᵢ, vᵢ₊₁)(x − vᵢ) that vanishes on the line through edge i, and two simp lemmas unfold it. So it is an internal coordinate device for the polygon-edge machinery, not a standalone notion from the literature to judge for generality. The closest general analogue in Mathlib is the area form ω(q−p, ·) of an oriented 2-dimensional real inner product space (`Orientation.areaForm`), up to sign convention. The definition is correct for its purpose.
